name: org.machanism.machai:bindex-core
description: Bindex Core is a Java 17 library for describing reusable software components as Bindex v2 metadata and making that metadata discoverable to developers, AI agents, and MCP integrations. It validates and registers Bindex JSON descriptors, retrieves complete or field-selected metadata, and recommends libraries from natural-language requirements using classification embeddings, semantic vector search, language and architecture-layer filtering, relevance thresholds, and version selection. It includes AI-facing functional tools for metadata retrieval, library picking, registration from files, URLs, or in-memory JSON, schema access, and generation guidance. MongoDB is used as the Bindex repository, while configurable GenAI and embedding providers support semantic classification and search. The library is intended for Maven projects, Ghostwriter and gw-maven-plugin extensions, and Machai MCP Server deployments that require governed, observable reuse of indexed software libraries.

constructors.description: Creates an empty Bindex metadata summary. Set its identifier, version, description, and relevance score when representing a search, recommendation, or reporting result.

examples.description: Creates a summary record and populates the fields commonly returned for a relevant indexed library.

features.name: get-bindex
features.description: Retrieves a registered Bindex descriptor by artifact identifier, or reads a descriptor directly from an HTTP(S) URL or a project-relative file URL. The optional GraphQL-style selection query reduces the response to requested top-level fields, such as name, version, or classification.

examples.snippet: get-bindex id="file://bindex.json" graphql-query="{ name version classification { languages } }"
examples.description: Reads the local descriptor and returns only identity and language-classification information for a lightweight inspection.

features.name: pick-libraries
features.signature: java.util.Collection pick-libraries(java.lang.String prompt, java.lang.Double score, java.lang.Integer searchLimits)
features.description: Recommends indexed libraries for a natural-language development requirement. The tool uses vector search and returns candidates that meet the requested minimum relevance score; the default score is 0.85 and the default candidate limit is 25.

examples.snippet: pick-libraries prompt="I need Java components for AI-assisted library metadata discovery and semantic search" score=0.86 search-limits=10
examples.description: Finds a focused set of high-relevance Java libraries before designing an application or selecting dependencies.

features.name: register-bindex
features.description: Loads a Bindex descriptor from a project-relative file path or HTTP(S) URL, normalizes its schema reference, and saves or updates the record in the configured Bindex repository. When omitted, the path defaults to bindex.json.

examples.description: Registers the descriptor generated in the project root so it can participate in semantic library discovery.

features.name: register-bindex-json
features.description: Registers a structured Bindex JSON object already held by an agent or application, without requiring an intermediate file. The tool applies the Bindex schema reference before saving and returns the record identifier.

examples.description: Publishes metadata created in memory by an automated cataloging workflow; a production object must also include every required Bindex v2 field.

features.name: getBindexSchema
features.description: Provides the bundled Bindex v2 JSON Schema resource at file:///schema/bindex-schema-v2.json as UTF-8 application/json content. AI agents and MCP clients use this resource to verify required descriptor fields and value types before registration.

examples.description: Loads the authoritative schema resource before generating or reviewing a Bindex descriptor.

features.name: generate-bindex
features.description: Loads the bundled Markdown prompt template used to guide schema-compliant Bindex generation. It gives AI integrations reusable generation context for descriptors, classification data, and practical usage information.

examples.description: Retrieves the generation guidance before an agent assembles a descriptor from project documentation and build metadata.

customizations.name: BINDEX_REPO_URL
customizations.description: Configures the MongoDB connection URI used by the Bindex repository. Set it to a reachable MongoDB or MongoDB Atlas Local instance when using a local or dedicated metadata repository.

examples.description: Configures a Windows command-session client to use the documented local MongoDB repository credentials.

customizations.name: GenAI and embedding model configuration
customizations.description: The host application configures gw.model, pick.model, and embedding.model to classify requests and generate embeddings used for semantic library selection.

examples.description: Supplies model settings as JVM properties before launching an application that hosts Bindex Core.

examples.title: Use Bindex tools from a Machai MCP Server
steps: Download machai-mcp-server.jar and bindex-core.jar from the Machanism release pages.
Configure GenAI credentials and model properties for the environment.
Start the server with both JARs on the classpath and port 45000.
Connect an MCP client, discover the Bindex tools, then invoke get-bindex, pick-libraries, or register-bindex for a project workflow.
examples.description: Windows command example. Keep credentials outside source control and use a colon rather than a semicolon as the classpath separator on Unix-like systems.

examples.title: Add Bindex Core to an application
steps: Declare Bindex Core as a Maven dependency using the published version appropriate for the consuming project.
Configure MongoDB repository connectivity and the GenAI and embedding provider in the host application.
Generate and validate a bindex.json descriptor for each reusable library.
Register descriptors, then use the library-picking tool to find components for new requirements.
examples.description: This scenario establishes a repeatable metadata catalog and semantic discovery workflow for Maven-based development.
